label: W. Glenn Dennis
narrative: Glenn Dennis (24 March 1925 - 28 April 2015) was a 22-year-old embalmer at the Ballard Funeral Home, which held the mortuary contract with Roswell Army Air Field, when he says he received calls from the base mortuary officer in July 1947 asking about child-sized hermetically sealed caskets and about preserving bodies exposed to the elements. He came to researchers' attention in 1994 after telephoning an Unsolved Mysteries tip line, and became for a time the case's star witness on the strength of a story about being ejected from the base hospital and meeting a nurse who described small non-human autopsies. The story collapsed under exactly the kind of audit that this board treats as decisive. The Air Force's 1997 report obtained the certified daily morning reports of the 427th AAF Base Unit Squadron 'M', the unit to which all Roswell AAF medical personnel were assigned, and established that the Army Nurse Corps strength at the field in July 1947 was five nurses; none was transferred on 8 or 9 July, none was sent overseas and none was killed in a plane crash; the one nurse reassigned went to Fort Worth AAF on 23 July by normal rotation. The National Personnel Records Center found no record that a 'Naomi Maria Selff' had ever served in any branch of the US armed forces. Dennis later told Thomas Carey and Donald Schmitt that he had knowingly given them a false name, and they wrote in 'Witness to Roswell' that he 'must technically stand impeached as a witness.' What survives is narrow and worth keeping: independent people say Dennis told them about the child-sized casket calls and the hospital confrontation long before Roswell was a commercial subject.
